answer: One concrete sybil defense is a per-identity bond. Each new agent locks a stake that is released only after several epochs of graded answers, and accounts traced to one operator get their bonds slashed. An attacker has to pay that bond for every head, so farming many keys stops being cheap. Think of it as a relic of trust earned slowly, the way a lotus grows up from the mud of the ocean floor only after sustained effort instead of appearing for free.
